title: Census of India 2011: Paper 1 of 2018 - Language: India, States and Union Territories (Table C-16: Population by Mother Tongue)
authors: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India

title: Census of India 2011: Special Tables for Scheduled Tribes (Table ST-14 / Primary Census Abstract for Scheduled Tribes)
authors: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India
publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, New Delhi

Documents 46,489 Gaddi Scheduled Tribe population in Jammu & Kashmir across Kathua (19,414), Udhampur (14,357), Doda (9,878), Kishtwar (1,326), Ramban (846), and Reasi (382). title: The Gaddi Scheduled Tribe of Jammu & Kashmir: A Socio-Cultural Overview
publisher: Govt Degree College Bhaderwah / Academic ResearchGate Repository
notes: Socio-cultural and anthropological overview of Gaddi ST settlements in Doda/Bhaderwah/Assar. Documents pastoral life, transhumance shelters (Hadwari), handlooms (Khade), and wool production. Does NOT provide descriptive linguistic lexicon.

title: Socio-cultural Analysis of Gaddi Tribe: A Sociological Study of Saraj Area in Jammu Region
publisher: International Journal for Multidisciplinary Research (IJFMR), Vol. 6, Issue 1
notes: Sociological study of the Gaddi community in the Saraj area of Doda district. Documents transhumance, pastoral leadership (Maalak), and material culture. Does NOT provide descriptive linguistic lexicon.

title: Blessed by Lord Shiva: The Gaddi Tribe of Jammu and Kashmir
publisher: Jammu & Kashmir Arts Foundation
notes: Cultural documentation of J&K Gaddi heritage, transhumance, Shaivite Nawala ritual, and traditional garments (Chola, Dora). Does NOT provide descriptive linguistic lexicon.

title: The Gaddi Tribe of Himachal Pradesh: A Sociological Study
publisher: Sterling Publishers, New Delhi
notes: Authoritative anthropological monograph on Himachal Gaddi pastoralism, customs, and kinship.

title: Saraz: Lok Aur Parampara and Duggar Ka Itihas
publisher: Kitab Mahal / Regional Academic Publishers, Jammu
notes: Regional folkloric background of Duggar and Saraz hill tracts. Unverified lead; lacks linguistic phonetic transcriptions or dedicated Gaddi lexical fieldwork.

authors: Jammu and Kashmir Academy of Art, Culture and Languages

title: Jambu: A Digital Comparative Dictionary of the Indo-Aryan Languages (Gaddi Reflexes)
publisher: Digital CLDF database (moli-mandala / Oxford University Press)
underlying_sources: T. Grahame Bailey (1908), The Languages of the Northern Himalayas
Sir George A. Grierson (1916), Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX, Part IV
license: Database code MIT; source dictionary text subject to copyright (OUP / SOAS)
notes: Reports 1,118 historical Indo-Aryan etymological reflexes for Gaddi (code ga). Audit confirms coordinates map to Bharmaur, Himachal Pradesh, and underlying data derives from Bailey (1908) and Grierson (1916). Exactly zero forms originate from Jammu & Kashmir. Quarantined as comparative_only.

title: Linguistic Survey of India: Himachal Pradesh
authors: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India
publisher: Office of the Registrar General, India (ORGI), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, New Delhi
underlying_sources: Fieldwork in B.P.O. Bharmaur Tehsil, District Chamba (Informant: Shri O.P. Verma)
notes: Official post-independence Linguistic Survey of India (LSI) report for Himachal Pradesh, published in 2023 by the Office of the Registrar General, India (ORGI). Based on Language Division field surveys conducted between 1995 and 2008 in B.P.O. Bharmaur Tehsil, District Chamba (primary language informant: Shri O.P. Verma). Contains Chapter 2 (Bharmauri/Gaddi descriptive grammar, phonology, morphology, syntax, and narrative text, pp. 58-119) and Chapter 6 (Comparative Lexicon across mother tongues including Bharmauri/Gaddi, pp. 1089-1100). Although introductory notes acknowledge Gaddi settlements in Jammu & Kashmir, all linguistic elicitation in this survey is strictly Himachal Pradesh Bharmauri baseline (hp_chamba_bharmaur).

title: Kinship Analysis of Gaddi: A Sociolinguistic Study
notes: Research study on Gaddi kinship terminology and sociolinguistics in J&K. Full text was investigated across AMU AJL volumes 11-15, Glottolog, Shodhganga, and ResearchGate; confirmed as currently unhosted/inaccessible in open-access repositories. Preserved as a high-priority research lead.
